statement.p: Find the critical point of the function f(x,y)=x^{2}+y^{2}+3xy-5x

Use the Second Derivative Test to determine whether the point is
test fails
a local minimum
a local maximum
a saddle point

static.solution:
f(x,y)=x^{2}+y^{2}+3xy-5x equal to zero and solve f_x(x,y)=2x+3y-5=0 f_y(x,y)=2y+3x=0 The second equation implies that y=-1.5x. Substituting into the first and solving for x gives: 2x - 1.5x - 5=0 \Rightarrow x=-2 The corresponding value of y is y=-1.5(-2)=3. The critical point is (-2,3).
Now we compute the Discriminant. We find the second-order partials: f_{xx}(x,y)=2 \quad f_{yy}(x,y)=2 \quad f_{xy}(x,y)=3 The discriminant is D(x,y)=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2=2\cdot 2-(3)^2=-5
Applying the Second Derivative Test we have D(-2,3)=-5 \lt 0 The Second Derivative test implies that f(-2,3) is a saddle point.
